'''Gregory C. Fu''' is an American chemist who is a professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he is the Norman Chandler Professor of Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gregory C. Fu {{!}} Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering|url=https://cce.caltech.edu/people/gregory-c-fu|access-date=2021-07-03|website=cce.caltech.edu}}</ref> The current research interests of the Fu laboratory include metal-catalyzed coupling reactions and the design of chiral catalysts.  In particular, the group is focused on the development of nickel-catalyzed enantioselective cross-couplings of alkyl electrophiles and on copper-catalyzed carbon–heteroatom bond-forming reactions. The group works in collaboration with the laboratory of Professor [[Jonas C. Peters]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fu |first1=Greg |title=The Fu Group, Publications |url=http://fugroup.caltech.edu/2015ndashpresent.html |website=The Fu Group, Publications}}</ref>

In 2014, he was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite news | title= April 29, 2014: NAS Members and Foreign Associates Elected | url= http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-29-2014-NAS-Election.html | publisher= National Academy of Sciences | date= April 29, 2014 | accessdate= August 19, 2015 | url-status= dead | archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20150818062140/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-29-2014-NAS-Election.html | archivedate= August 18, 2015 }}.</ref>  He was awarded an [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]] in 1998–1999.<ref name="American Men & Women of Science" />
He was awarded the [[Elias J. Corey Award]] from the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2004.

Professor Fu is also the inventor of the ferrocene analogous [[Fu's Planar DMAP|planar DMAP]] catalyst.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ruble |first1=J. Craig |last2=Tweddell |first2=Jennifer |last3=Fu |first3=Gregory C. |date=1998-05-01 |title=Kinetic Resolution of Arylalkylcarbinols Catalyzed by a Planar-Chiral Derivative of DMAP: A New Benchmark for Nonenzymatic Acylation |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jo980183w |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |volume=63 |issue=9 |pages=2794–2795 |doi=10.1021/jo980183w |issn=0022-3263|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Education==
Gregory Fu received his B.S. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1985, where he worked in the laboratory of Professor [[Karl Barry Sharpless]], then completed his Ph.D. at [[Harvard University]] in 1991 under Professor [[David A. Evans]].<ref name="American Men & Women of Science" /> He worked as a postdoctoral fellow with [[Robert H. Grubbs]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1991 to 1993, before accepting an assistant professor position at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where he worked from 1993 to 2012. In 2012, he was appointed the Altair Professor of Chemistry at Caltech. Fu is currently the Norman Chandler Professor of Chemistry at Caltech.

==Awards and honors==
* Received the [[Elias J. Corey Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2004
* Received the [[Mukaiyama Award]] of the [[Society of Synthetic Organic Chemistry of Japan]] in 2006
* Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 2007
* Received the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|Award for Creative Work in Synthetic Organic Chemistry]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2012
* Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]], 2014
* Received the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|Herbert C. Brown Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2018
* Received the [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|Arthur C. Cope Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2026
